content: To create a new page on WikiDoc, you must be a registered user. If you are not registered, you need to register before proceeding. Before creating a new article, it is crucial to search WikiDoc to ensure that a page on your topic does not already exist. To search for a specific word or topic on WikiDoc, type the desired term into the search box located on the main page and press the Search button. If the page exists, you will be directed to it. If not, you will see a list of pages containing the term. Review these pages carefully, as relevant information may be categorized under a different topic. Next to the Search button, you will find the Try Exact Match button. This feature narrows the search to pages with the exact name you entered. If you know the precise name of the page you are looking for, this option allows you to go directly to it without navigating through links. If no suitable page exists for your topic, you can create a new page. After searching, if the topic is not found, you will see a prompt to Create the page 'Topic name' on this wiki. Click on the topic name to begin creating the page. You will be directed to the edit page for the new topic. If you are adding a new disease, copy and paste the text from the Template to add a New Disease page. This ensures uniformity across WikiDoc pages and automatically generates a table of contents for your page. To use the template, click the Edit button at the top of the template page, select all the content, and copy it. Then, return to the edit page of your new topic and paste the copied content. Insert the relevant information into the appropriate subtopics. Once you have completed your edits, click Save Page below the edit box. You can monitor changes to your page by clicking the Watch tab at the top of the page. This allows you to track any additions or edits made by others. To create a user page, which serves as your identity page on WikiDoc, click the link provided in the instructions. This page allows you to introduce yourself to the editing community and is a space for creative expression. To create a WikiDoc Board Review Question, ensure that all questions are original and do not violate WikiDoc's plagiarism policies. Any copyright violations are the responsibility of the question's creator. Board review questions are reviewed by WikiDoc Scholars on Monday mornings and must be approved by the Editors-in-Chief before being uploaded. To create a Crowd Diagnosis page, the goal is to assist patients and doctors in diagnosing elusive conditions. WikiDoc has compiled the largest repository of known causes of symptoms, signs, and laboratory abnormalities. These lists are initially generated using artificial intelligence for sensitivity and then verified by human intelligence for specificity. The process is rigorous but facilitated by the contributions of physicians worldwide. To create a Critical Pathways page, these are evidence-based multidisciplinary management tools for specific patient groups with predictable clinical courses. Critical pathways improve care quality, reduce costs, and shorten hospital stays. WikiDoc supports this initiative and provides instructions for creating such pages. To create a Guidelines page, the purpose is to summarize the latest science and management recommendations to improve healthcare quality. This project is intended for medical professionals at all levels and implements an evidence-based approach to medical advances and treatment guidelines. To create a Microchaptered page, a chapter on WikiDoc is composed of smaller sections called microchapters. For example, the disease pericarditis is divided into microchapters such as Pericarditis Overview, Pericarditis Pathophysiology, and Pericarditis Treatment. Microchapters enhance accessibility and maintain consistency across WikiDoc pages. To create a Resident Survival Guide page, this project is a collaborative effort to address common medical conditions encountered by medical graduates in training. It aims to enhance the diagnostic and treatment skills of residents and house staff while following evidence-based approaches to public health conditions. To create a Patient Information page, this type of page is patient-oriented and typically addresses the background, diagnosis, and treatment of a condition. For editing a created page, refer to the editor's tool page for guidance on creating references, redirects, and links. If you wish to edit an existing page, you can contribute constructive edits to improve the content. Use the How to edit a page guide for assistance.
